results.title: Could NYC see a new record for days without rain?
excerpts:
# Could NYC see a new record for days without rain?
NEW YORK (PIX11) — Very dry conditions around New York City have raised concerns, specifically the [high risk of fire](https://pix11.com/news/local-news/red-flag-warning-issued-for-nyc-area/) starting or spreading due to high winds.

...

[More Local News](https://pix11.com/news/local-news/)
**When was the last time it rained in NYC?**
According to the [National Weather Service](https://www.weather.gov/okx/) , the last time precipitation was recorded in the New York City metro area was Sept. 27.
The dry spell could potentially end this week as [scattered showers are forecasted](https://pix11.com/weather/warm-halloween-possible-in-ny-nj/) for Friday. However, if the forecast changes, New York City may see a new record for consecutive days without precipitation.
**What is the record?**
The [longest record of days without precipitation](https://www.weather.gov/media/okx/Climate/CentralPark/ConsecutiveDayswithwithoutPrecip.pdf) in New York City since 1869 is 36 days, according to the National Weather Service. The record was set in the autumn of 1924.

results.title: When Will It Rain in New York? City’s Driest Fall Ever, Explained
excerpts:
# New York City Is Having the Driest Fall in History
New York’s exceptionally dry autumn is unprecedented. A combined 1.59 inches of rain was recorded in Central Park in September and October, the lowest since records were kept starting in 1869.

...

That 29-day streak with no rainfall is the second longest in the city’s history; the longest streak was a century ago in 1924, lasting 36 days in October and November.

# When will it rain in NYC? City on track for driest October in history
## An entire month without rain (so far)
The last time New York City experienced any measurable rainfall was Sept. 30, according to [AccuWeather](https://www.accuweather.com/en/weather-forecasts/record-dry-conditions-spark-wildfire-fears-across-northeast-and-mid-atlantic/1706316) .

excerpts:
# Historic NYC dry streak comes to an end — sort of. How does the record stack up?
## An “excellent shot” at breaking another record
Additionally, we still have a chance of breaking the record for the driest month in city history. Currently, the driest month in New York City was June 1949, which only featured 0.02 of an inch of rain, according to the NWS.
